name: MD4
notes: Collisions found; practically broken. Historical interest and legacy protocol (e.g. NTLM) only.

name: MD5
notes: Practical collision attacks since 2004; chosen-prefix collisions demonstrated. Unsuitable for security; still seen as a non-security checksum.

name: SHA-0
notes: Withdrawn shortly after publication due to an undisclosed flaw; superseded by SHA-1.

name: SHA-1
notes: Collision demonstrated in 2017 (SHAttered); chosen-prefix collision in 2020. Deprecated by NIST (SP 800-131A) and browsers.

name: SHA-224
notes: SHA-2 family; truncated SHA-256 with different initial values.

name: SHA-256
notes: SHA-2 family; widely used (TLS, Bitcoin, package signing). No known practical weaknesses.

name: SHA-384
notes: SHA-2 family; truncated SHA-512. Resistant to length-extension attacks.

name: SHA-512
notes: SHA-2 family; 64-bit word operations, faster than SHA-256 on 64-bit CPUs.

name: SHA-512/256
notes: SHA-2 family; SHA-512 truncated to 256 bits with distinct IVs; immune to length extension.

name: SHA3-224
notes: FIPS 202; Keccak sponge, rate 1152 bits. Different construction from SHA-2, so a structural break in one does not affect the other.

name: SHA3-256
notes: FIPS 202; Keccak sponge, rate 1088 bits.

name: SHA3-384
notes: FIPS 202; Keccak sponge, rate 832 bits.

name: SHA3-512
notes: FIPS 202; Keccak sponge, rate 576 bits.

name: SHAKE128
notes: FIPS 202 extendable-output function (XOF); arbitrary-length output, 128-bit security strength.

name: SHAKE256
notes: FIPS 202 extendable-output function (XOF); arbitrary-length output, 256-bit security strength.

name: RIPEMD-160
notes: No practical collisions known; used in Bitcoin/Ethereum address derivation. Less analysed than SHA-2.

name: BLAKE2b
notes: Faster than MD5 while secure; digest configurable up to 512 bits, 1024-bit internal block. Optimised for 64-bit platforms.

name: BLAKE2s
notes: BLAKE2 variant for 8–32-bit platforms; digest configurable up to 256 bits, 512-bit internal block.

name: BLAKE3
notes: Highly parallel Merkle-tree hash; default 256-bit digest, extendable output. Much faster than BLAKE2/SHA-2.

name: Whirlpool
notes: ISO/IEC 10118-3 standard; based on a modified AES block cipher. Not widely deployed.

name: CRC32
notes: Error-detection checksum, NOT a cryptographic hash; trivially forgeable. Included for reference to avoid misuse.
